summary: Unallocated prepayment posted to vendor account generates suspense balance and blocks invoice matching
description:
Issue summary: A €48,250 prepayment (bank reference RB-20260309-9987) was posted to vendor ledger for vendor 'Nordic Data Supplies' (VND-4472) but was not allocated to the open invoice INV-2026-0345. The AP system shows a prepayment/suspense GL code instead of an AP-credit that can be applied, resulting in an outstanding invoice on the supplier portal and a reconciliation mismatch for March bank close.

Impact: Blocks automatic 3-way match for PO-987245, prevents supplier from being marked settled, causes month-end unreconciled suspense of €48,250 (affects cash position reporting). Finance close window at risk if not resolved.

Environment: Production AP ledger (NetAcct v4.2) integrated with payments gateway (PayGrid); AP batch 2026-03-09-09:00 CET. Region: eu-west.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Payment file generated by Payments team for vendor VND-4472 on 2026-03-09.
2) Bank confirmed debit on 2026-03-09 09:12 CET (RB ref above).
3) NetAcct processed incoming payment feed and created prepayment record using GL 2995-suspense instead of GL 2100-AP-credit.
4) Matching engine did not auto-apply to INV-2026-0345 due to missing vendor application rule (expected behaviour: auto-apply when PO match found).

Logs / evidence: Bank statement excerpt (s3://redwood-finance/evidence/2026-03-09/RB-20260309-9987.pdf), AP processing log snippet (ap-processor-2026-03-09.log lines 412-428), NetAcct audit trail (audit-trail-VND-4472.csv). Slack thread: #fin-ap (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02FINAP123).

Immediate business workaround requested: reverse suspense entry, repost as AP credit and apply to INV-2026-0345; then re-run reconciliation for March close.

Recommended long-term action items: Add a mapping validation that rejects prepayment to suspense when vendor and invoice are both present in the batch; add alert for single prepayment >€10k to create manual review task; review PayGrid -> NetAcct mapping for remittance reference parsing.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Oliver Grant: Filed after noticing unreconciled bank debit during daily cash report. Attached bank PDF and AP processing log.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Maya Rodriguez: Assigned to AP ops. Initial hypothesis: mapping rule failed to detect invoice reference in remittance. Will attempt manual allocation and capture steps.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Systems Engineer (Liam Park): Confirmed payment file contained remittance field 'PO:987245;INV:INV-2026-0345' — parser returned empty invoice_id due to unexpected delimiter. Uploaded parser error lines to ticket.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Maya Rodriguez: Performed manual journal reversal and reposted as AP credit. Applied credit to INV-2026-0345. Vendor portal now shows invoice settled. Posted reversal TXN ID: JR-2026-03-12-557.
2026-03-13 10:05 - Finance Manager (Amir Khan): Confirmed month-end reports updated; suspense balance cleared. Requesting permanent fix to parser and test coverage added to integration tests.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Engineering Lead (Priya Patel): Parser PR merged and scheduled for 2026-03-16 staging deploy. Added a validation rule to reject ambiguous remittance formats.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: remittance parsing edge-case — delimiter ';' vs expected '|' produced null invoice_id in mapping layer.
NetAcct created prepayment because incoming payment record had vendor ID but missing matched invoice_id field; fallback path uses GL 2995-suspense.
Payment gateway (PayGrid) sometimes formats remittance differently for vendors sending consolidated files; no prior alert existed for >€10k prepayments.
Confirmed that auto-apply engine requires both vendor_id and invoice_id to be present; adding guard to attempt fuzzy-match on remittance when invoice_id missing.
Related historical ticket INT-34121 documented a similar mapping mismatch for a different vendor in 2025 Q4; root cause was parser robustness.
resolution: Manual reversal and repost completed on 2026-03-12 (JR-2026-03-12-557). INV-2026-0345 marked settled and suspense GL cleared. Engineering deployed parser fix to staging (PR merged 2026-03-14) and scheduled production deploy for 2026-03-16 after smoke tests. Finance requested monitoring rule for prepayments >€10k and a follow-up audit to close any other lingering suspense entries. Owner for follow-up: Maya Rodriguez.
follow_up_actions: Prod deploy parser fix on 2026-03-16 - Engineering
Add alert for prepayments > 10000 EUR - Finance Ops
Quarterly sweep for suspense GL entries - Finance Ops
